title: feat(automation)!: an approval decision resumes a flow as the person who decided
body:
Fixes #24321

Clause-②: yes (narrowing). The narrowing: under `runAs: 'user'`, a post-decision node that the submitter's rights admitted and the decider's do not is now refused (ruling A item 3). The widening: three published interfaces each gain one optional member, `ResumeSignal.resumedBy` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`) and the `resumedBy` field on `ApprovalResumeSurface`'s resume signal and on `StrandedContinuationSignal` (`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`). No schema shape moves: `flow.runAs` keeps its two values and only its describe changes.

After an approval decision (approve or reject), the flow's following nodes run as the person who decided: ruling A (comment 6257886738), with item 2 read on its measured population by ruling 6267719791 (Q1 A, Q2 A).

## What changes

- **`runAs: 'user'`: identity and permissions together.** On resume, `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` builds the context the nodes after the pause run with. When the service-stamped signal names a decider (`resumedBy`), the context is a copy of the persisted one with the trigger user's `positions`, `permissions` and `org_user_ids` removed, `userId` set to the decider, and the decider's own grants resolved by `seedRunGrants`. That is the trigger setup's resolver from PR #24495, now shared by both callers.
- **`runAs: 'system'`: keeps system privileges, and the attribution user becomes the decider** (ruling 6267719791 Q1 A). The nodes after the decision run as `{ isSystem: true, userId: DECIDER }`, the shape the approvals verdict mirror already writes with. No grant is resolved and elevation is unchanged, so a `readonly` verdict column still lands. The trigger user's grants are removed here too, so `current_user` in the segment is the decider. `updated_by`, `sys_audit_log` and `ctx.user` in the hooks those writes fire name the decider.
- **Both postures.** A later pause persists the switched context, so a second decision, a cold resume or a resume with no decider continues from the decider's segment and never falls back to the submitter. `SeededRunContext.triggerUserId` keeps the run's trigger, so the run history (`buildRunTrigger`) still names who started it.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`.** `decide` hands `resumedBy: actingUserId(context)` to the engine, the person the verdict mirror already writes as. The SLA sweep's `SYSTEM_CTX` vouches for nobody, so its auto-decision names no decider and the run keeps its identity. A stranded decision journals its decider, and `continueRestoredRun` replays it as them. The row builders (#24501's region; #24519 now queued on them) and the hand-built `{ isSystem: true, userId }` write contexts are untouched.
- **Safety.** The engine honours a decider only beside `RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE`. The REST resume body is also a closed key set (`inputs`, `variables`, `output`, `branchLabel`), so an HTTP caller cannot send a decider at all.
- **Unchanged:** flows with no human decision node; SLA auto-decisions, on both postures; a subflow parent's own nodes (the parent declares no decision node); and the send-back, resubmit and recall doors (ruling 6267719791 Q2 A: only approve and reject carry the decider).

## Measurement (ruling A item 5)

### HotCRM's four branches: who holds the write each post-decision node makes

Read only, `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` at `296167936b06` (pinned to `@objectstack/*` 18.0.0-next.3). Rep = `sales_rep` (`src/sales/profiles/sales-rep.profile.ts`); manager = `sales_manager` (`src/sales/profiles/sales-manager.profile.ts`). Object edit and row policy are the same on every row: the manager holds `crm_opportunity: { allowEdit, viewAllRecords, modifyAllRecords }` (`sales-manager.profile.ts:22`) under the `select` row policy `opportunity_private_owner_only` (`:117`–`:127`, `is_private == false || owner_id == current_user.id`); the rep holds `allowEdit` with `readScope: 'own'` (`sales-rep.profile.ts:52`). Neither set carries a field entry for any column below.

| branch | node | field(s) | manager holds it | rep holds it |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `opportunity_approval` approve | `mark_approved` | `approval_status`, `approved_date` | **no**: both `readonly: true` (`opportunity.object.ts:485`, `:498`) | **no**, same |
| `opportunity_status_change_approval` approve | `apply_status` | `stage`, `status_change_approval_status`, `approved_date` | `stage` yes; the other two **no**: `readonly: true` (`:549`, `:498`) | `stage` yes on own deals; the other two **no** |
| `opportunity_status_change_approval` reject | `clear_request` | `status_change_approval_status`, `requested_status` | `requested_status` yes; the verdict **no**: `readonly: true` (`:549`) | `requested_status` yes on own; the verdict **no** |
| `opportunity_qualification_approval` reject | `clear_request` | `qualification_approval_status`, `qualification_requested` | `qualification_requested` yes; the verdict **no**: `readonly: true` (`:215`) | `qualification_requested` yes on own; the verdict **no** |

Every one of these nodes writes a `readonly: true` column, which objectql strips from every non-system UPDATE (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, the `if (!opCtx.context?.isSystem)` branch of the UPDATE path). So **all four branches need elevation**, and all four flows already declare `runAs: 'system'` (`opportunity-approval.flow.ts:57`, `opportunity-status-change-approval.flow.ts:70`, `opportunity-qualification-approval.flow.ts:72`). So do the other two HotCRM approval flows (`account-approval.flow.ts:75`, `lead-conversion-approval.flow.ts:66`). Recorded per item 3 as the pull for a finer, per-node elevation: the ordinary fields (`stage`, `requested_status`, `qualification_requested`) could then go through the manager's own rights while the verdict and stamp columns land as platform writes.

Under ruling 6267719791 Q1 A, this PR now reaches all four branches. They keep their elevation, and their post-decision writes name the manager (next table). The in-repo `showcase_invoice_signoff` (`runAs: 'system'`, a post-decision `update_record`) is met with them.

### After the change: attribution, and the run's report when a right is missing

Measured through the real doors, on the harness HotCRM's own suites boot (`@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack`, `requires: ['automation', 'triggers', 'approvals', 'audit', 'sharing']`). The fixture mirrors HotCRM's shapes: a `private` deal object with HotCRM's `readonly` `approval_status` and `approved_date` columns; a rep set (`allowEdit`, `readScope: 'own'`); a manager set (`allowEdit`, `viewAllRecords`, `modifyAllRecords`, with `restricted_note` non-editable); a `record-after-create` flow with a position-routed `approval` node and a post-decision `update_record` on each branch. The rep creates the deal with `POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT`; the manager decides with `POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/ID/approve` or `/reject`. It was a one-off measurement file, deleted after each run; the permanent pins are listed under Tests.

| flow (`runAs`) | decision | `updated_by` before → after | `sys_audit_log` update row | readonly column | run | door |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `system` (HotCRM shape) | approve | rep → **manager** | `{approval_status, approved_date}` by **manager** | `approval_status: approved`, `approved_date` set | `completed` | 200 |
| `system` (HotCRM shape) | reject | rep → **manager** | `{requested_status, approval_status}` by **manager** | `approval_status: rejected` | `completed` | 200 |
| `user` | approve | rep → **manager** | `{approved_note}` by **manager** | (not written) | `completed` | 200 |
| `user` | reject | rep → **manager** | `{requested_status}` by **manager** | (not written) | `completed` | 200 |
| `user`, the manager lacks the field | approve | rep → rep (nothing landed) | none | (not written) | `failed` at `post_approve`: `[Security] Field write denied: not permitted to edit [restricted_note] on 'OBJECT'` | 500 `RESUME_FAILED`, `repairable: true`, naming the request, the run, the node and the denial |

All five rows were measured at `c17394ee5`, the final head. The rep's own `create` row stays theirs in every case. A pre-decision flow node keeps the submitter too: in the service-automation real-stack test, the `submit` node leaves `updated_by` and its audit row on the rep, on both postures.

## Rulings

Open questions from the first round are **ruled: `6267719791`, Q1 A, Q2 A** (maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-19T12:55Z). Q1 A: a `runAs: 'system'` flow keeps system privileges, and after the decision its attribution user is the decider. Q2 A: send-back, resubmit and recall keep item 1 as written.

## Tests

At `c17394ee5`:
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/resume-decider-identity.integration.test.ts` (new, 21 pins; 1.32 s of test time).
  - Envelope, read off a recording node that captures `resolveRunDataContext(context)`. `runAs: 'user'` approve and reject carry the decider's resolved grants and none of the submitter's. A later pause keeps the decider; a second decision moves to its own decider while the run history keeps the trigger; a decider whose grants fail to resolve runs on the baseline.
  - Envelope, `runAs: 'system'`: approve and reject carry `{ isSystem: true, userId: usr_mgr, positions: [], permissions: [] }` with no grant resolved and the forwarded grants removed, and the run history keeps the trigger.
  - Envelope controls: a system run with no decider keeps the rep; a decider without the service marker, no decider, and no decision node are all unchanged.
  - Real stack (ObjectQLPlugin, driver-sql, identity objects, SecurityPlugin, SharingServicePlugin, AuditPlugin). `runAs: 'user'`: `updated_by` and the `sys_audit_log` row name the manager after and the rep before; a guard shows the manager's write rests on the manager's own sets; an FLS-denied post-decision node is refused as a repairable strand naming the node and field, while the same node with no decider lands as the rep. `runAs: 'system'`: a guard shows the `readonly` `verdict` column is stripped from the manager's own request; approve and reject land `verdict` under the unchanged elevation, with `updated_by` and the audit row naming the manager; with no decider, the rep.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/restored-approval-continuation.test.ts` (one describe, 6 pins, on the file's existing pinned engine double, through the real `ApprovalService` and `approval` node). `decide` approve and reject run a `runAs: 'user'` flow's post-decision nodes as the decider with the decider's grants, and a `runAs: 'system'` flow's as `{ isSystem: true, userId: u1 }`. The SLA-shaped decision keeps the run's identity. A stranded decision journals `resumedBy: 'u1'`, and `continueRestoredRun` replays as the decider.
- Suites at `c17394ee5` (after merging `origin/main` to `04669a467`): `@objectstack/service-automation` `pnpm test` 192 files / 2567 passed; `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `pnpm test` 81 / 1118 passed; `@objectstack/spec` `pnpm test` 701 / 21311 passed (1 todo). `typecheck` is green for all three (`check:test-typecheck` OK, debt ledgers unchanged).
- `packages/services/service-automation/package.json` gains `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` as devDependencies (lockfile: 6 lines), each aliased to source in `vitest.config.ts`. A `private` object's write verdict belongs to record sharing, and the audit row is the audit plugin's.

## Ablation (one-off, not kept)

Both runs went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `engine.ts`. The suite imports the engine relatively, from source, so no build or dist leg applies. Each direction was predicted before its run.

- **Round 0, the whole switch.** The decider read was replaced with `undefined` (blob `7172068a6966` → `6dfa06c97035`). Predicted red on the decider pins; observed **8 failed / 6 passed** of the 14 then present. Restored: `blob == HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Round 1, the system half.** `|| context?.runAs === 'system'` was added to the early return (anchor hit 1 → 0; blob `019ddb6c6fd5` → `0a62cc66e57a`). Predicted red on exactly the four system attribution pins; observed **4 failed / 17 passed**. Failed: envelope system approve and reject, and real-stack system approve and reject. The system no-decider controls and the history pin stayed green. Restored: `blob == HEAD 019ddb6c6fd5`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates

Local, at `c17394ee5`, after the final commit: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 127 families over this diff. All 127 were run, each recorded `:: exit 0`. `--ran` reconciliation: **127 derived, 127 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**. The local-only `check:dev-prereqs` is OK. The changeset gates on the new text: `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` OK (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, read as BREAKING + bang + clause-② narrowing), with `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-empty-changeset` OK. An earlier start of this round's union was stopped and re-run from scratch after `packages/spec` was rebuilt: a comment-only edit had left its `dist` stale, and the fresh worktree lacked 21 package builds. CI's check-runs on this head are the seat's to read.

**Round 2 (contract review `6270059532`, rework `6270117310`), head `e5150923a`.** This round changes no code: two sentences of `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, and the decider pin file's header comment, which now names `restored-approval-continuation.test.ts`. `origin/main` was merged to `2667e2402` (`e5150923a`, via `os-regen-merge.sh`); its six commits touch no package this PR changes. The derived list was re-derived on the final diff (127 families) and run in full: every family `:: exit 0`, and `--ran` gives **127 derived, 127 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**. `check:dev-prereqs` and `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` are OK. The decider pin file runs 21/21 at `e5150923a`. The full package suites were last run at `c17394ee5`, as listed above.

## Spec-lane files

Declared to the spec seat (`contracts/**` included, per ruling 6267719791 item 3):
- `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`: the `runAs` describe and its comment (ruling A item 2's sentence, and item 2's new reading for `'system'`).
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`: `ResumeSignal.resumedBy` (new optional member, both postures in its TSDoc); the TSDoc of `AutomationContext.userId`; and the parity sentence under `AutomationContext.flowName`, which now says the acting user moves to the decider on both postures.
- Regenerated by `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix` (`gen:docs`, the one artefact it proved stale): `content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx`, `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`.

## Acceptance notes

- A strand journalled before this release carries no `resumedBy`, so its repair replay continues as the trigger user. A run that paused before this release and is decided after it does switch. Carrier: none.
- A subflow-hosted approval switches the child run only; the parent continues with its own context. The parent declares no decision node, so this follows item 1's last sentence. Carrier: none.
- No ADR records a ruling on the resumed identity (`docs/adr` searched: ADR-0019, ADR-0044, ADR-0073, ADR-0118). ADR-0073 D2 (posture is not attribution) is the closest, and the system posture now follows it: elevation is posture, the decider is attribution. Per item 6 no ADR line is owed, and none was written.
- The hand-written flows guide (`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`) now says what the describe says, after contract review `6270059532` found two sentences this PR had made false (rework `6270117310`). The `runAs` row reads: `'system'` is elevated, and after an approval decision its attribution user is the decider; `'user'` is the trigger user until a human decision and the decider after it. The "Who may resume" paragraph reads: a resumed run continues under the identity stored on the run, the user who started it or, after an approval decision, the decider. The caller gate after it (`trigger.userId`) is unchanged. `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` was found true and is unchanged.
- A hook that reads `ctx.user` on a write a `runAs: 'system'` approval flow makes after the decision now sees the decider. HotCRM's opportunity guards key on `ctx.user?.id` being present, which stays true; the changeset says so.
